subject.title: Feature: Inject context window % into system prompt runtime section

question: Should OpenClaw expose passive context-window usage in the system-prompt Runtime line, and what exact freshness and display contract should it use?
rationale: The source path is clear, but adding volatile per-turn context metadata changes prompt semantics and cache behavior, so automation should not choose percentage-only versus token counts, stale-snapshot omission, previous-turn semantics, or model-switch behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
options.body: Add a small context field below the cache boundary using only fresh or explicitly documented previous-turn usage, with tests for stale, compaction, and model-switch behavior.

options.title: Keep explicit inspection only
options.body: Leave context usage on `/context`, `/status`, `session_status`, and diagnostics surfaces, then close or update this issue once maintainers decide passive prompt metadata is not desired.

options.title: Defer to runtime self-context design
options.body: Keep this narrow request blocked on the broader runtime self-context plan instead of landing a Runtime-line primitive now.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
recommendation.body: Add a small context field below the cache boundary using only fresh or explicitly documented previous-turn usage, with tests for stale, compaction, and model-switch behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history signal for the Runtime prompt contract and is the best available owner for a product boundary decision.
